subject: Background-job SLA carveout and retry modes for async inference
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@orchard.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai; procurement@orchard.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: SLA for background/async inference jobs - clarification

Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks for the call earlier — Orchard is very close to finalizing the integration for our nightly de-identification pipeline. Before we sign the purchase order we need a short written confirmation about how Redwood will treat asynchronous/background inference jobs for SLA purposes. The procurement team sent a short PDF with our requirements (attached). High-level asks:

- Job completion window guarantees (preferred 24 hours end-to-end for queued batch jobs, with defined retries)
- Idempotency guarantees so we don't double-process records if retries happen
- How retries/backoff are handled and whether retries count against throughput/SLA units
- Any credits or carve-outs if a job misses its completion window due to transient infrastructure issues

Can you provide a firm statement we can include with the PO or, if you need exceptions, an alternative commitment?

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Director of Data Ops
Orchard HealthTech

[Attachment: orchard_sla_req_20261102.pdf (application/pdf, 142 KB)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@orchard.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA for background/async inference jobs - clarification

Maria — appreciate the note and the PDF. Quick summary from our side and a proposed carveout so you can forward to procurement: 

1) Completion window
- For async/batch inference we guarantee job completion "best-effort" within a 24-hour window for standard Dedicated customers under normal operating conditions.
- For Hosted/Shared capacity we aim for a 24-hour completion window but the contractual SLA is scoped to a 48-hour completion window for large (>10M records) jobs unless Reserved Burst is purchased.

2) Retry and idempotency behavior
- Redwood supports idempotency tokens at the job-level. If a job is re-submitted with the same job_id/idempotency_token within a 7-day dedup window, we will not re-process records already marked completed.
- Per-record dedup: for jobs that send per-record identifiers, we will perform dedup checks at ingest time; if you rely on client-side idempotency only, duplicate requests within the dedup window will be ignored.

3) Retries/backoff and impact on SLA units
- Automatic retries for transient infra errors are attempted with exponential backoff (initial 10s, max 5m) and do not count against your compute credits separately — they are part of the job execution.
- If retries cause a job to exceed the committed completion window, we will classify the incident under "completion window breach" and follow the credits policy below.

4) Credits / carve-outs
- For Hosted customers: if a job fails to complete within the contractual window due to platform unavailability (Redwood-controlled outage), we provide a credit of 10% of the monthly inference spend for the affected job batch up to a cap of 50% for recurrent failures.
- For infrastructure issues caused by third-party cloud provider maintenance or force majeure, we provide a partial carveout and will propose a remediation plan; credits in these cases are at Redwood's discretion.

5) Operational recommendations (optional)
- Use per-record identifiers and our per-record retry policy when possible; this reduces reprocessing risks.
- If you need stricter windows, consider Dedicated with Reserved Burst for large nightly windows.

I've looped in Dev (cc) to add the technical details on token semantics and exactly how the dedup window behaves. Please confirm if the Hosted vs Dedicated carveouts are acceptable and whether we should include this language in the SOW.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_response_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 34 KB)]

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@orchard.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA for background/async inference jobs - technical details on idempotency and retries

Maria / team — quick technical note to clarify the runtime behavior Jon raised: 

- Idempotency token scope: tokens are scoped at the job_id level (string) and at the per-record id (optional). If you provide both, the runtime first deduplicates at the job level, then at the per-record id.

- Dedup semantics: we keep a tab of completed record ids for 7 days by default; this window can be extended to 30 days for Dedicated customers with an agreed retention delta. After the retention window, identical job submissions may re-process records.

- Exactly-once vs at-least-once: Redwood's default processing model for async jobs is effectively at-least-once with dedup safeguards (idempotency tokens + per-record id matching). We can enable stricter "exactly-once" behavior for critical pipelines by enabling an optional acknowledgement layer and durable write-backed checkpointing; this is a Dedicated feature and adds ~5-15% latency to job completion depending on job size.

- Retries: automatic retries are per-failed request fragment; they are bounded and capped to prevent runaway reprocessing. We track retry attempts in the job execution trace and expose counts in the job detail page in the Console.

- Failure taxonomy and credits: only incidents classified as Redwood-controlled (service faults) will be considered for SLA credit. Upstream failures (your network, customer misconfiguration) will be documented but not eligible for credits.

If helpful, I can provide a short example payload and sequence diagram of token handling for your integration team.

— Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@orchard.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA for background/async inference jobs - finalize language for SOW

Maria — thank you, this is helpful. From Legal/Contracts: we can include the 24/48-hour completion windows and the credit structure Jonas proposed. A couple of small edits we will include in the SOW: 

- Define "Redwood-controlled outage" explicitly (service-side incidents resulting from Redwood runtime/hypervisor/kernel faults, not third-party infra maintenance).
- Add an exclusion for customer-supplied malformed payloads and rate-limit breaches.
- For Dedup window expansion requests (7 -> 30 days) we'll include an addendum with retention costs.

If that sounds ok to you, I'll prepare a short SOW addendum and ask procurement to sign an acknowledgement. Once we have the signed PO I will route for final approval on our side.

Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
